t: Marine brine - ancient
s: Modern seawater is a Na–(Mg)–Cl–(SO4) water, with a density of 1.03 gm/cc and salinity around 35 ± 2‰. When seawater evaporates, a predictable suite of primary evaporite salts crystallise from increasingly concentrated hypersaline waters. As seawater concentrates, the first mineral to precipitate is CaCO3, usually as aragonite. This begins in mesohaline waters where the brine reaches twice the concentration of seawater (40 to 60‰) and achieves a density ≈1.10 gm/cc.
